articles.headline: Wayne Rooney wouldn't 'feel comfortable' accepting Premier League medal if Man City stripped of titles
articles.description: Wayne Rooney has said he wouldn't feel comfortable being handed another Premier League medal if Manchester City are stripped of their title win in the 2011-12 season.
articles.body:
Wayne Rooney has said he wouldn't "feel comfortable" being handed another Premier League medal if Manchester City are stripped of their title win in the 2011-12 season.

City are expected to be found guilty of breaching over 100 of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

Their sanctions are yet to be announced for the alleged financial misconduct but the possibility of the club being stripped of the titles they won during this nine-year period.

They won three Premier League titles in this time, the first of which saw them pip Manchester United on goal difference in the 2011-12 season.

Rio Ferdinand, who was a member of this United team that finished second, has laid claim to Premier League medal but Rooney hasn't followed suit.

"I have heard Rio has come out saying about getting another Premier League medal ... I wouldn't really feel comfortable accepting another Premier League medal, if I'm being honest," he said on his podcast Stick To United.

"I don't think we deserve it, we didn't do enough that season to win the league. I think we were six or seven points clear with four or five games to go and we threw it away. The amount of time which has been between it, to accept a Premier League medal ....

"I've seen everything that has come out over the past few days and listening to people and I was putting myself in a Man City player's shoes. They are there, doing everything to win a Premier League title and in their minds, they have done it, they have won the Premier League title.

"if that happened to me, if all of a sudden Manchester United had been doing the same and my Premier League medaI had been taken away from, I would be absolutely devastated.

- Joe Hart: I believe Man City chairman claims that club are innocent

- 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports

"It might happen, they might take them away, but I wouldn't want it because I don't think as a team we deserved it that year because obviously we didn't finish first. So when I see ex-teammates and other people saying 'I want a medal' ... I'm happy with the five I've won. I wouldn't want this one, just 15 years later you get a medal because City cheated.

"Should they get it stripped for what the owners have done? Yeah maybe, but I wouldn't feel comfortable accepting it."

articles.headline: What has gone wrong for the Patriots' offense, Drake Maye?
articles.description: New England is last in the NFL in offensive points per game at 9.7. Can Maye and his supporting cast settle things down and turn it around?
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had committed his third turnover, which was quickly turned into a touchdown, and was preparing to take the field again late in the third quarter of Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jaguars.
Before he did, there was a moment on the sideline with head coach Mike Vrabel, who looked directly into Maye's helmet as he wrapped both of his arms around the quarterback's shoulder pads, play-sheet still in his left hand. Vrabel was doing his best to uplift Maye, whose start to the season has unexpectedly spiraled downward with six interceptions and a lost fumble. The defending AFC champions are now 1-2 heading into Sunday's road game against the 3-0 Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, CBS).

What has happened to Maye?

He had said his comfort level entering the second season in coordinator Josh McDaniels' offense was high, but he has looked mostly uncomfortable -- which has led to poor decision-making, defenses successfully pressing him and myriad miscues as he has navigated injuries to No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown and other core players around him. Maye called the offense "unacceptable" -- the unit ranks last in the NFL in points per game (9.7) -- and said he planned to "look in the mirror and take this as a turning point."

Vrabel cited a golf analogy in identifying one place for him to start.

"I think sometimes, we really want to make a good score, right? Sometimes we're so focused on it, we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we're squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways," Vrabel said on sports radio WEEI.

"We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren't there."

Maye's struggles have contributed to the Patriots scoring the third fewest points through three games by a reigning conference champion in the Super Bowl era; their 36 trail only the 1999 Falcons (28) and 2007 Bears (33) Their 0.97 points per drive makes them the first team with less than one point per drive through three games since the 2021 Jets quarterbacked by Zach Wilson. And their minus-0.21 EPA per play is the worst by any team through three games since the 2023 Jets.

Teammates and coaches have consistently mentioned that the team's early-season challenges aren't solely on Maye, though.

"I think this is just an offensive unit deal, a team thing," receiver Romeo Doubs said. "The fundamentals are key ... fundamentals aren't strong enough. I keep emphasizing on it because that's part of this league, this game. You cannot win games doing your own thing. You have to have some sort technique and some professional initiative to get things rolling."

articles.body:

articles.headline: Patrick Vieira reveals Manchester United, Sir Alex Ferguson talks during Arsenal stint
articles.description: Patrick Vieira has revealed he had the opportunity to join Manchester United as a player.
articles.body:
Patrick Vieira has revealed he had the opportunity to join Manchester United as a player.

The France midfielder made his mark for Arsenal in the Premier League, arriving in north London in 1996 and winning three titles during his nine years there, including captaining the "Invincibles" team in 2003-04.

But Vieira has said he had the chance to join Sir Alex Ferguson's Manchester United, Arsenal's regular title rival during that period.

In an interview with Sky Sports, Vieira said: "I had the opportunity to move to Real Madrid a couple of times and I even had ... An opportunity to move to Manchester United.

"I had a meeting with Sir Alex Ferguson. Full respect, I couldn't say no to meeting him because he was an important figure in the Premier League. We met and we talked and he explained to me his vision that he had for Manchester United and the team that he wanted to build.

"He wanted to play me with Roy Keane, [Ryan] Giggs on the left-hand side, David Beckham on the right-hand side and [Paul] Scholes to play behind [Ruud] Van Nistelrooy, so it wasn't a bad team.

"But I couldn't leave Arsenal, I was too happy there and we were on the way of building something quite really special for the club and that's the way it was.

"When you do well, of course there's teams who are interested and then you have to make a decision. But the decision for me was to stay at Arsenal because I felt the love from the club, from the players and from the fans. Everything was there for me to grow up as a player and to achieve what I wanted to."

- Havertz back at Arsenal for treatment after injury on Germany duty

- Cantona 'wouldn't have joined' Man United under Jim Ratcliffe 

- Man United selling chunks of Old Trafford pitch

Vieira eventually left Arsenal in 2005 and had stints with Juventus and Inter Milan before finishing his career with Manchester City.

He then went into management and has had spells at New York City, Nice, Crystal Palace, Strasbourg and Genoa and, now 50, is currently head coach of Senegal.

articles.headline: Man City CEO adamant legal battle with the Premier League is not over - reports
articles.description: Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has told his fellow European club bosses the already lengthy legal battle with the Premier League will take "a lot more time" to conclude.
articles.body:
Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has told his fellow European club bosses the already lengthy legal battle with the Premier League will take "a lot more time" to conclude.

News broke on Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of 115 charges they faced of breaching the league's financial rules, immediately sparking speculation they could face unprecedented sanctions.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak told supporters in an open letter published on Saturday that the club were "confident" of proving their innocence, and chief executive Soriano addressed the elephant in the room when he met fellow members of the European Football Clubs board in Copenhagen on Monday.

The Press Association understands Soriano said at the end of the EFC board meeting that he felt he had to say something given Friday's news, that City disagreed with the ruling but remained confident of winning and that the club were still fighting.

Sources in the meeting said Soriano then remarked: "It's taken eight years to get here, and it's going to take a lot more time."

The "eight years" Soriano referred to was the opening of the league's investigation into City in 2018.

Soriano, who declined to answer media questions as he exited the meeting, made the comments in the presence of some other English top-flight bosses, with Manchester United's chief of international football relations Jean-Claude Blanc and Everton owner Dan Friedkin -- there in his capacity as owner of Roma -- also attending the meeting in the Danish capital.

Among the alleged breaches, all strenuously denied by City, was a charge of failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini's pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

The 61-year-old, now in back in charge of Italy for a second stint, was quizzed about the charges at a press conference ahead of Monday's Nations League match with Turkey in Bursa.

He said: "It's not an issue that concerns me. It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years."

The Premier League has declined to comment since news of the verdict emerged last week, and Mancini continued: "Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

City were charged with failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons from 2009 -- the year Mancini took over.

They were also charged with failing to provide full details of remuneration in contracts with players between 2010-11 and 2015-16, and with failing to co-operate with the Premier League's investigation over a period from 2018 to 2023.

A City spokesperson said on Friday: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

articles.headline: Joe Hart: I believe Man City chairman claims that club are innocent
articles.description: Former Man City goalkeeper Joe Hart has said he trusts club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak's claims that the club will "prove their innocence" despite the expectation they will be found guilty of the majority of breaches of Premier League financial rules.
articles.body:
Former Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart has said he trusts club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak's claims that the club will "prove their innocence" despite the expectation that they will be found guilty of the majority of breaches of Premier League financial rules.

ESPN reported on Friday that City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of the 115 charges. Although the Premier League have not commented on what it calls a "private and confidential process," City have not denied the guilty verdict and have said that the process "remains ongoing."

In a statement published on Friday, Al Mubarak said that "nothing has changed" regarding the club's legal battle with the Premier League and added that "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

Hart, who played for City between 2006 and 2016, told BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club that he has "nothing but love and respect" for Al Mubarak.

"I've heard everyone else go down every single rabbit hole, every single wormhole, every single discussion and be given free rein to say whatever they want about something that hasn't been proven," Hart said.

"My honest opinion is I've got no reason not to trust Khaldoon... He's been excellent with everything that he's done with Manchester City... I've got nothing but love for the club, nothing but love for him, nothing but respect for him.

"I realise it's opened up a can of worms. I realise it's opened up what ifs and buts and maybes and how and who... But when there's speculation in the air, it's just speculation.

"My genuine feeling, as someone who played for the club, is that I'm going to have to let it play out... But for me, someone who I trust, someone who's led me and led the club brilliantly, what he said is enough."

- Man City CEO adamant legal battle with the Premier League is not over

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports

Hart was adamant that "nothing concrete" has happened yet with regards to this legal battle reaching a conclusion.

"I loved how he [Al Mubarak] spoke. I loved the letter because that was from someone who cared about the club.

"I can't get involved in the ifs and the buts and the maybes. If Man City are found guilty, which I don't think they are because of what Khaldoon said, then there are conversations to be had.

"But right now, I'm very confident and I'm very calm. I'm very proud of what I achieved with Man City and what we achieved as a team. And that doesn't change. That doesn't change until you tell me otherwise."

articles.headline: Soccer's best 2025-26 kits: The most stylish jerseys you probably missed
articles.description: While the world's top clubs release their new kits on a wave of hype, there are many more who release absolutely banging jerseys that deserve to be seen.
articles.body:
While the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and all of the Premier League big hitters have their new kits released on a wave of hype, they make up just a small percentage of the soccer jerseys on sale each season.

For every European heavyweight's flashy, expensive launch campaign, there are hundreds of smaller clubs world who have put just as much effort and ingenuity into their new kit concepts and designs for a much smaller audience.

So after casting a discerning eye over the various home, away and third shirts released for the 2026-27 season, we feel it our sworn duty to help showcase some of the finest, most brilliant and super-stylish concepts that have been rolled out by clubs at all levels of the game over the past couple of months.

- Soccer's wildest warmup kits: The good, the bad and the ugly

- A kit fit for the GOAT: Messi's special kit for Argentina farewell

- Premier League 2026-27 kits: Ranking every jersey released

Here, in alphabetical order, is our considered pick of some of the best football kits that you might not have had the pleasure of seeing until now.

Ajax away (Adidas)

Dutch giants Ajax have added yet another beauty to their ever-increasing catalogue of handsome alternative kits. Predominantly black and burnished gold, this shirt also features an elaborate light grey graphic incorporating outlined images of nine of the club's most significant historic achievements; from their four European Cup/UEFA Champions League titles to winning their 30th Eredivisie shield in 2011.

Angers away (Nike)

Exquisite silver-on-silver design from the Ligue 1 side who have used a cool, retro Total 90 template to create a rather special away kit akin to a suit of gleaming futuristic titanium armor.

Atalanta away (New Balance)

This season sees the return of a classic for Atalanta, who have successfully resurrected their glorious white away kit of the late 1980s and early '90s. The modern incarnation retains the zigzag graphic of the original, but reapplies it across the chest with a touch of added contemporary panache.

Celta Vigo third (Hummel)

Celta have traipsed back through their archives in search of inspiration and settled on a gorgeous red diamond pattern inspired by their cult classic 1995-96 "harlequin print" away kit. While still positively oozing with retro appeal, the modern take is even sweeter.

Como home (Adidas)

Como are very much the new kids on the block in the Serie A style stakes, and this season they will be bringing their elegant aesthetic to the Champions League. In essence, the home jersey is a classic polo-style design in blue which mirrors the color of the water of the famous Lake Como. The lines are incredibly clean and the red, white and gold tricolore trim ices the cake perfectly.

FC Basel third (Macron)

articles.headline: Bears call on QB3 Case Keenum in rousing victory over Eagles
articles.description: In his first NFL start in 1,009 days, Chicago third-string quarterback Case Keenum, 38, led the Bears to a dominant 27-7 victory over the perennial NFC heavyweight Philadelphia Eagles on Monday, a performance coach Ben Johnson labeled "extraordinary."
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- The night belonged to Case Keenum. And so did a game ball.

After leading the Chicago Bears to a dominant 27-7 win over the perennial NFC heavyweight Philadelphia Eagles on Monday, which marked his first start in 1,009 days, Keenum was handed the commemorative football and the floor in the postgame locker room at Soldier Field.

With quarterbacks Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent looking on behind him, Keenum delivered a passionate postgame speech about his 67th career start. He talked about how his opportunities to play meaningful football had routinely been taken away and how he rediscovered his love for the game after coach Ben Johnson persuaded him to come out of retirement and be a part of Chicago's quarterback room in 2025.

With Williams dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring strain that is expected to keep him out three to four weeks and Bagent not clearing the NFL's concussion protocol until Sunday, the Bears turned to their third-string quarterback to get their second win of the season.

"It's all about Case Keenum and what he was able to do here tonight," Johnson said. "I thought he did an extraordinary job."

At 38 years and 223 days old, Keenum became the second-oldest quarterback in franchise history to win a start (Todd Collins has him beat by 116 days). Chicago's 20-point win was its largest on "Monday Night Football" since Week 15 of the 2010 season at the Vikings.

Keenum didn't resemble a backup quarterback who was trying to keep his team afloat in the absence of its starter. He accounted for three touchdowns and zero turnovers in the win, leading Chicago on an 11-play, 66-yard opening drive that ended with Keenum finding Luther Burden III for an 8-yard touchdown.

Keenum later connected with Kalif Raymond on a 41-yard touchdown late in the third quarter and dove into the end zone on a 1-yard quarterback sneak. Keenum has won games as a starting quarterback with seven different franchises, tying his former Texans teammate Ryan Fitzpatrick for the most in NFL history.

"Playing well anytime in your career feels good," Keenum said. "To do it on 'Monday Night Football' after you thought you weren't ever going to play again multiple times. Golly, this is special. It's really special. And I don't know if I'll be able to put it into words tonight, but I'm going to enjoy it tonight, that's for sure."

Keenum orchestrated an offensive performance that relied on its passing attack. As the Eagles focused on stopping Chicago's run game, Keenum completed 24 of 34 attempts for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.

He showed poise in the face of pressure. Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio sent 12 blitzes, and the results were disastrous for the Eagles: Keenum finished 11-of-11 for 145 yards and two touchdowns when the Eagles sent additional rushers.

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. articles.headline: Sirianni regrets reaction to hit on QB Hurts in Eagles' loss
articles.description: After a 27-7 loss to Chicago on Monday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni expressed "remorse" over his reaction to a sideline hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson on Philadelphia's Jalen Hurts that temporarily knocked his quarterback out of the first half.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni expressed "remorse" over his reaction to the sideline hit by Chicago Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson on Jalen Hurts that temporarily knocked his quarterback out of the game midway through the second quarter Monday night.

Cameras showed Sirianni appearing to shout expletives toward Jackson after the play.

"Obviously, you want to always fight for your players, and protect your players. I always come away when I have a moment like that with remorse of, 'Man, I shouldn't have let my emotions get the best of me,'" Sirianni said after the Eagles' 27-7 loss.

Facing a second-and-4 deep in Chicago territory, Hurts scrambled to the right sideline and began stepping out of bounds by the first-down marker. Jackson hit him hard in the shoulder area, sending Hurts crashing to the turf, and was whistled for unnecessary roughness.

Hurts got up and rejoined his teammates, but the referees stepped in and directed Hurts off the field to be tested for a concussion.

Andy Dalton took over at quarterback and threw an interception on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, denying the Eagles their first points of the game.

"I apologized to [Hurts]," Dalton said. "I put us in a bad spot, but I put him in a bad spot, too."

Hurts left the medical tent to watch the third-down play unfold, but he had not yet been cleared. Moments later, he received the go-ahead to return to action. Hurts was visibly upset as he exited the tent and made his way toward the bench.

"I was just waiting for the thumbs-up. I felt fine; we already checked it," he said. "I don't know the extent of the process; obviously, wish we could have expedited things. I know I felt fine."

Sirianni said, "I get nothing," when asked what type of information he was receiving about Hurts' status in that moment. "They need to go through their process there. You think about maybe calling a timeout in a situation like that ... but if you call a timeout, I have no idea what's going on and when he's going to come out.

"I think that's the right way to go about it because you don't want to influence anything. The health of the player is the most important thing."

Hurts returned the following series and orchestrated an eight-play, 67-yard drive that he capped with a tush push touchdown as time expired in the opening half. That proved to be the final points the Eagles scored on the night.

Sirianni had a different perspective on the pivotal hit on Hurts postgame compared with his initial reaction.

"Those guys are out there trying to make a play. It was close on the sideline, ended up being a penalty," Sirianni said. "Obviously, you never want to see your quarterback get hit like that, but it's in the heat of the moment. I know nobody is trying to hurt anybody out there, and I always have remorse when I act that way. But I always love fighting for our players.

"I have to be more steady in that situation. ... I didn't like how I handled that."
